canonical_name: Highest-weight classification theorem family for semisimple Lie algebras
literal_source_claim_zh: 半单李代数不可约表示由最高权分类
literal_source_claim_en: Irreducible representations of semisimple Lie algebras are classified by highest weight.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only a classification gloss. It omits finite-dimensionality of the Lie algebra and representations, scalar field and characteristic, splitting assumptions, Cartan/Borel and positive-root choices, weight lattice and dominant-integral predicate, Lie-module and irreducibility encodings, isomorphism-class representation, whether classification includes existence and both uniqueness directions, and all boundary cases. Selecting a familiar complex or algebraically-closed-field formulation at intake would add proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: the selected source must fix the scalar field and universe, characteristic and algebraic closure, finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra, Cartan/Borel and positive-root data, representation carrier and universe, finite dimensionality, irreducibility, weights, and isomorphism-class parameter space.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not say whether the root asserts existence of a highest weight, uniqueness of the weight, construction and uniqueness of a simple module for each dominant integral weight, a bijection on isomorphism classes, or a sourced conjunction.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is source-selected; scope-map.md lists the required boundary decisions.
candidate_scope_not_credited: finite-dimensional irreducible complex modules of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra are parameterized up to isomorphism by dominant integral weights relative to chosen Cartan and positive-root data
the same parameterization over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field under explicit splitting hypotheses
existence and uniqueness of the highest weight for each finite-dimensional irreducible module
construction of the unique finite-dimensional simple module L_lambda for each dominant integral weight via a Verma-module quotient
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: zero Lie algebra, empty root system, zero highest weight, trivial and one-dimensional modules
zero module versus the nonzero condition implicit in irreducibility
semisimple direct sums and repeated isomorphic modules
infinite-dimensional irreducible modules and finite-dimensionality of the Lie algebra and module
reductive algebras with center and simple versus semisimple algebras
non-algebraically-closed or positive-characteristic fields and nonsplitting Cartan data
dependence on Cartan, Borel, positive-root, and simple-root choices
group representations versus Lie algebra modules and the integration/simply-connected boundary
excluded_substitutions: classification of simple Lie algebras, Dynkin diagrams, or root systems
complete reducibility, Lie's theorem, Engel's theorem, weight decomposition, or Cartan existence alone
the universal property of Verma modules or uniqueness of a simple quotient without occurrence and finite-dimensionality classification
compact Lie group representation classification without a checked group-to-algebra transport
affine Kac-Moody, category O, quantum-group, finite-group, or arbitrary infinite-dimensional module classification
abstract predicates or structures storing the desired highest-weight classification as input
generic semisimple, Cartan, root-system, weight-space, or enveloping-algebra APIs alone
legacy S1_M_053 affine predicate data or the catalog's untrusted verified label
